You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE museum (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Num_of_Staff INT,
    Open_Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visitor (
    ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Level_of_membership INT,
    Age INT,
    UNIQUE (ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visit (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    visitor_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Num_of_Ticket INT,
    Total_spent REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (visitor_ID) REFERENCES visitor(ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Museum_ID) REFERENCES museum(Museum_ID)
);

To get **frequent museum visitors**, you first need to define what “frequent” means (e.g., **at least N total visits**, or **visited at least N different museums**).

Here are the common SQL options—pick the one you want:

### 1) Visitors with at least N total visits (most common)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS total_visits
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5;   -- change 5 to your threshold
```

### 2) Visitors who visited at least N different museums
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) AS museums_visited
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) >= 3;  -- change 3 to your threshold
```

### 3) Top K most frequent visitors (ranked)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS total_visits
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
ORDER BY total_visits DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

Which definition do you want: **(a)** total visits, **(b)** different museums, or **(c)** top-ranked list? And what threshold (N) or top K?
look for visitors who have gone to museums a bunch of times

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5      -- “a bunch” threshold; change as needed
ORDER BY num_visits DESC;
```

If you tell me what “a bunch” means (e.g., 3+, 10+), I can set the `HAVING` value accordingly.
just focusing on visitors to museums

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  v.ID,
  v.Name
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
ORDER BY v.ID;
```
also need to think about people who have been to these museums

If you mean “list each museum and the people who have visited it,” use:

```sql
SELECT
  m.Museum_ID,
  m.Name AS museum_name,
  v.ID AS visitor_id,
  v.Name AS visitor_name
FROM museum m
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.Museum_ID = m.Museum_ID
JOIN visitor v
  ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY m.Museum_ID, v.ID;
```

If instead you want “people who have visited a specific museum (by Museum_ID)”, tell me the Museum_ID and I’ll tailor the query.
I need the unique IDs of these visitors too.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  v.ID AS visitor_id
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
ORDER BY v.ID;
```

If you also want the museum they visited (still unique pairs), use:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  vi.Museum_ID,
  v.ID AS visitor_id
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
ORDER BY vi.Museum_ID, visitor_id;
```
gotta get the names of the visitors too

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  v.ID AS visitor_id,
  v.Name AS visitor_name
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
ORDER BY v.ID;
```
also need to get the ages of the visitors too

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  v.ID   AS visitor_id,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Age  AS visitor_age
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
ORDER BY v.ID;
```
